Megjegyezzük végül, hogy a vogulban általában a szó első tagjára esik a főhangsúly s a harmadikra a mellékhangsúly. ... Ép úgy mint a magyarban az igekötő elenyészteti az alapszó hangsúlyát s hasonlóképpen a tagadó és tiltó szócskák is az utánuk következő igéét, vagy igeszerű névszóét. Ez általános hangsúly-törvénytől csak a tavdai nyelv tér el sok tekintetben, ezért ebben a hangsúlyt minden egyes szón külön jelzem. It is the only stress statement in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent the : no other 'stress/accent' hits except the gloss 'distress'). Surrounding section read (30.1-30.2.5): the chapter explicitly describes Middle Konda (KM) with Lowe…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the first syllable; a rhythmic secondary stress falls on the following odd-numbered syllables (3rd, 5th). Stated for East (Konda) Mansi; Honti 1988: 151 states the same primary-stress rule in his description of Pelym (West) Mansi ('Die Betonung im Wogulischen ist dynamisch und liegt regelmäßig auf der ersten Silbe'), and Munkácsi 1887-90 (NyK 21: 325-326) gives it for all Vogul dialects except Tavda ('a vogulban általában a szó első tagjára esik a főhangsúly s a harmadikra a mellékhangsúly.. Ez általános hangsúly-törvénytől csak a tavdai nyelv tér el' = 'in Vogul generally the main stress falls on the first syllable of the word and the secondary stress on the third.. only the Tavda language deviates from this general stress law').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on odd-numbered non-initial syllables (Forsberg 2022); 'on the third syllable' (Munkácsi NyK 21: 325); Munkácsi NyK 23: 396 ties the Konda infinitive allomorphy (-γw in 2nd/4th vs -aγw in 3rd syllable) to this secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None in Forsberg 2022 or Honti 1988. Munkácsi (NyK 21: 326) adds that verbal prefixes take the stress off the base verb and negative/prohibitive particles off the following verb (phrase-level destressing), and that only Tavda (Southern Mansi, sout3253, not part of cent2322) deviates from the first-syllable law. Kulonen/Forsberg's English grammar notes phonetic shortening of first-syllable long vowels in closed syllables and before a long second-syllable vowel, without linking it to stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement (isolated word forms as transcribed in Kannisto's Konda texts); Munkácsi's remarks on prefixes and negative particles concern stress groups (hangsúly-egység) in connected speech.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog's 'Central Mansi' (cent2322) unites East Mansi (Konda: east2879, subdialects KU lowe1460, KM midd1374, KO uppe1481, Jukonda juko1234) and West Mansi (west2976: Pelym pely1234, Middle Lozva midd1373, Lower Lozva lowe1459, N/S Vagilsk). The quoted statement (Forsberg 2022) describes East Mansi, chiefly Middle and Lower Konda as recorded by Kannisto c. 1901-06 (language now extinct). Honti 1988: 151 gives the same first-syllable rule in a sketch of Pelym (West Mansi, pely1234), and Munkácsi 1887-90 states it for all Vogul dialects except Tavda (= Southern Mansi, sout3253, outside cent2322). Northern Mansi (mans1258) is a separate Glottolog language already handled elsewhere.

new_statements.quote: Bei der bezeichnung der akzent- und quantitätsverhältnisse habe ich mich im allgemeinen an das von Setälä vorgeschlagene System angeschlossen. Der exspiratorische akzent (hauptakzent) wird nur dann besonders angegeben, wenn ihn nicht die erste silbe des wortes trägt. [pp. XIV-XV] ... Ich habe meine betrachtung hauptsächlich auf die qualitative Seite der vokale beschränkt, da die quantität und die betonung sich am besten in sonderkapiteln in einheitlichem zusammenhange darstellen lassen [p. V] ... Die reduzierung des vokals im anlaut der unbetonten ersten silbe des wortes hat sich in den mundarten TJ, TČ weiter entwickelt als in Wörtern mit konsonantischem anlaut. [p. 55]
new_statements.translation: In marking accent and quantity relations I have in general followed the system proposed by Setälä. The expiratory accent (main accent) is indicated specially only when it is not borne by the first syllable of the word. [pp. XIV-XV] ... I have restricted my treatment mainly to the qualitative side of the vowels, since quantity and stress are best presented in separate chapters in a unified context [p. V] ... The reduction of the vowel in the onset of the unstressed first syllable of the word has developed further in the dialects TJ, TČ [Tavda: Janytchkova, Chandyri] than in words with consonantal onset. [p. 55]

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog's initial-stress record and with Forsberg 2022 (primary stress on the first syllable): Kannisto's convention treats first-syllable main accent as the unmarked default for the Konda and Pelymka/Vagilsk/Lozva material. It is a transcription convention rather than a descriptive rule, so it confirms but does not independently prove the placement; it says nothing about secondary stress on odd syllables.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The book has no stress chapter (stress and quantity are explicitly deferred to future separate chapters), but its transcription convention states that the main (expiratory) accent is marked only when it is NOT on the first syllable, i.e. first-syllable main stress is the unmarked default for Mansi as transcribed across all dialect groups covered (Tavda, Konda, Pelymka-Vagilsk-Lozva, Sosva-Upper Lozva). The only explicit non-initial-stress remark concerns the Tavda dialects (TJ, TČ), not the Central (Konda/Pelym/Vagilsk/Lozva) dialects.
new_statements.exceptions: Non-initial main accent is possible and is marked with a special sign when it occurs (convention, pp. XIV-XV); reduction/loss of the vowel of an 'unstressed first syllable' is noted for the Tavda dialects TJ, TČ (p. 55), i.e. a Southern Mansi variety outside cent2322; p. 21 and p. 59 speculate on earlier stress relations ('frühere betonungsverhältnisse') as an explanation for vowel alternations, without stating a rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Kannisto 1919 covers the whole Mansi dialect continuum recorded 1901-1906 (pp. IV-V): S-group Tavda (TJ, TČ, TG), Ö-group Konda (KU Unter-Konda/Nahrachi, KM Mittel-Konda/Leush, KO Ober-Konda/Saim), W-group Pelymka (P), Süd-/Nord-Vagilsk (VS, VN with VNZ, VNS, VNK), Unter-/Mittel-Lozva (LU, LUT, LM), N-group Ober-Lozva (LO) and Sosva (So). The Ö- and W-groups are the varieties Glottolog groups as Central Mansi (cent2322); the stress convention is stated for 'Wogulisch' generally, not per dialect.

sources.note: Introduction pp. 325-326 (verified on page scan NyK21_Munkacsi_p325-343/): in Vogul generally main stress falls on the first syllable and secondary stress on the third; verbal prefixes and negative/prohibitive particles take the stress off the following word; only the Tavda dialect deviates, so stress is marked per word only in Tavda. Munkácsi's own 1888-89 fieldwork covered N, Middle Lozva, Lower Lozva, Pelym, Konda, Tavda.

tone.quote: 1.4. Betonung Die Betonung liegt im Mansischen regelmäßig auf der ersten Silbe (Honti in Bezug auf PM 1988:151), so gehen wir davon aus, dass es im Pelym-Mansischen ebenfalls der Fall ist. [...] 2.4. Betonung Mit der Betonung beschäftigen wir uns hier ebenfalls nicht, siehe III.1.4.

tone.translation: 1.4 Stress. Stress in Mansi regularly lies on the first syllable (Honti with reference to Pelym Mansi 1988:151), so we assume that this is also the case in Pelym Mansi. [...] 2.4 Stress. We do not deal with stress here either, see III.1.4.
